canonical_refs.surface: Host-disk and SQLite pressure caused by agent actions (audit rows, approval rows, captures PNGs, docker commit snapshots, sources dirs) and by human read paths (GET /audit, /ui/audit, /ui/verify, /audit/verify, cmd_verify, GET /approvals)
canonical_refs.boundary: Agent-grown data -> one process-wide audit lock and one SQLite file shared by four connections (AuditLog, ApprovalStore, SandboxManager, DesktopControl). AuditLog.verify() and list() run fetchall of the whole table under the same lock that every append needs (agentbox/audit.py:196-215, 152-187). _safe_log swallows AuditWriteError after execution (agentbox/service.py:362-369), while _close_gui_burst has already popped the burst before logging gui_changes or gui_processes_stopped. ApprovalStore claim, finish and create raise raw sqlite3 errors (approvals.py:49-92), not AuditWriteError.
canonical_refs.subsystem: agentbox/audit.py#append + list + verify; agentbox/service.py#_safe_log + _close_gui_burst + decide + expire_stale; agentbox/approvals.py#create/claim/finish; agentbox/api.py#list_audit/verify; agentbox/web.py#verify_frag/audit_frag
canonical_refs.attack_class: Failure and recovery under resource exhaustion: read-side lock hold time and memory on the shared audit lock; fail-closed (503) versus fail-open (silently dropped post-hoc records, approvals stuck in approved) behaviour at disk-full or lock contention

canonical_refs.boundary: Network attacker with no token -> control-plane memory, the /tmp multipart spool, the Docker daemon and the audit chain. The tool-args body cap that critic checks only guard authenticated agent args. extract_novnc runs docker create, get_archive into memory and extractall per request (agentbox/sandbox.py:774-798, api.py:431-437).
